Alger, 14 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 14, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — SADID Diagnopharm Group and Mindray brought together Algerian and international specialists for the "Algeria Mindray Lab Forum 2026". The event focused on the contribution of artificial intelligence, diagnostic automation, and the connected hospital concept to the modernization of the national healthcare system.
Algeria Mindray Lab Forum 2026 — L'intel: Algeria Mindray Lab Forum 2026 — Artificial intelligence and the connected hospital at the heart of debates in Algiers
Organisée le 12 novembre 2026 à l’Hôtel: Organized on November 12, 2026, at the Sheraton Hotel in Algiers, the scientific conference entitled "Algeria Mindray Lab Forum 2026" gathered diagnostic professionals, key players in the medical sector, as well as national and foreign experts. The shared objective of the organizers is to support the technological transformation of Algerian healthcare facilities, focusing on laboratory digitization and the emergence of connected hospitals.
Les débats ont mis en avant la mutation: The discussions highlighted the transformation of medical biology laboratories through modern analytical tools. In hematology, the use of artificial intelligence supports human expertise through the automated analysis of cell morphology, enabling accelerated detection of abnormal cells and indicators of malignant hemopathies.
Les travaux scientifiques ont couvert pl: The scientific sessions covered several key disciplines, notably hematology, biochemistry, and immunology. The debates were moderated by Professors Mohamed Amine Moueden, Belaid Ait Abdelkader, and Amal Soulef Saadi-Ouslim.
La rencontre a également abordé le dével: The meeting also addressed the development of the connected hospital in Algeria. This model is based on the secure processing of medical data and the interconnection of equipment via integrated information systems. According to representatives of SADID Diagnopharm Group and Mindray, providing automation solutions and digital technologies aims to promote technology transfer, strengthen local skills, and align national hospital structures with international standards.
